zh: 长度可达三千万，2^(n−1) 种插法不可能逐一枚举。换个角度：把数字一位一位加进来，每个旧算式在新数字前只有两种选择——插一个加号让它自成新的一段，或者不插、把它接到最后一段的末尾。
只看前 i 个字符组成的全部算式，维护三个量就够了：算式个数 c、所有算式的值之和 f、所有算式最后一段的数值之和 g。插加号时值增加 d、最后一段变为 d；不插时最后一段 x 变成 10x+d，值增加 9x+d。
汇总两种延伸得到：c' = 2c，f' = 2f + 9g + 2cd，g' = 10g + 2cd；第一位数字时 c=1、f=g=d。从左到右扫一遍并全部对 10^9+7 取模，最后输出 f。输入很长，按块读取并跳过非数字字符，时间 O(n)、额外空间 O(1)。
en: The length can reach thirty million, so the 2^(n−1) ways of inserting cannot be enumerated one by one. Look at it differently: add the digits one at a time; before the new digit, each old expression has only two choices — insert a plus so the digit starts a new segment, or insert nothing and append it to the end of the last segment.

For all expressions over the first i characters, three quantities are enough: the number of expressions c, the sum of their values f, and the sum of their last-segment values g. Inserting a plus adds d to the value and makes the last segment d; not inserting turns the last segment x into 10x+d, adding 9x+d to the value.

Combining both extensions gives c' = 2c, f' = 2f + 9g + 2cd, g' = 10g + 2cd; for the first digit, c=1 and f=g=d. Scan once from left to right, doing everything modulo 10^9+7, and print f at the end. The input is long, so read it in blocks and skip non-digit characters; time O(n), extra space O(1).

explanationEn:
## Problem

Given a digit string num, you may insert '+' between any two adjacent characters (at most one '+' per gap, possibly none at all). Over all 2^(n−1) ways of inserting, evaluate the resulting expressions and find the sum of these values modulo 10^9+7. Each segment separated by '+' is evaluated as a decimal number, and leading zeros do not affect the value (for example, "05" has value 5).

## Prefix recurrence

Looking only at all expressions formed by the first i characters, maintain three quantities: the number of expressions c, the sum of the values of all expressions f, and the sum of the last-segment values of all expressions g. When the next digit d is added, each old expression extends in two ways:

- Insert '+' in between, and d becomes a new segment: the value increases by d, and the last segment becomes d.
- Do not insert '+', and d is appended to the last segment: the last segment x becomes 10x+d, and the value increases by 9x+d.

Summing up gives: c' = 2c, f' = (f + c·d) + (f + 9g + c·d) = 2f + 9g + 2cd, g' = c·d + (10g + c·d) = 10g + 2cd. Initially, with only the first digit, c=1 and f=g=d. The final answer is f.

## Correctness

Each expression of length i+1 corresponds uniquely to "an expression of length i + inserting or not inserting in the last gap". The two cases above cover exactly these two choices, and their effect on the value and on the last segment is computed by the decimal definition, so the recurrences for all three quantities are exact (they also hold modulo the prime, since only addition and multiplication are used). Induction up to the whole string gives the answer.

## Complexity

O(n) time and O(1) extra space. The reference reads the input in blocks, so even an input thirty million long needs only a single linear scan.

## Independent verification

The oracle starts from the contribution of each digit: the i-th digit (0-based), when it is the k-th digit from the right within its segment, contributes d·10^k; then the i gaps to its left are arbitrary, the k gaps from it to the end of its segment have no '+', the gap after the segment's end must have a '+' (unless the segment ends at the end of the whole string), and the remaining gaps are arbitrary. So the total weight of the i-th digit is 2^i·(Σ_{k<m} 10^k·2^{m−1−k} + 10^m) with m=n−1−i, accumulated from right to left, without reusing the prefix recurrence. For small domains, all ways of inserting are also enumerated and evaluated directly. Every digit string of length 1..4 is enumerated, and the reference program is actually run on each. The formal cases cover the original example, a single digit, all zeros, leading zeros, all nines, a random string of length thirty million and more. Four wrong programs that exit normally (not taking the count modulo, a wrong modulus, forgetting to add the new digit, missing the expressions that insert no plus) are each judged wrong on the formal cases.
